newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Mazda wants 2% of European market.
newsitem.headline: Mazda wants 2% of European market.

text.p: Mazda Motor Corp of Japan said it hopes to raise its market share in Europe to at least two percent from 1996's 1.3 percent.
Last year in Europe, Mazda raised its sales 4.8 percent to 169,000.
"We want to get to two percent as soon as possible," Mazda president Henry Wallace said in a speech at the Geneva car show to unveil the company's new VW Golf sized 323 range.

Mazda has been financially troubled until moving back into black ink recently. The strong yen, and its lack of production capacity in Europe pulled the company down. Vigorous cost cutting and agreement with its part-owner Ford Motor Co to produce some small cars for it in Europe were behind the turnaroud.
"Mazda definitely turned the corner last year in Europe after facing a few difficult situations," Wallace said in the speech.
Mazda sales had fallen for five consecutive years in Europe.
Wallace said that a sign of Mazda's new gusto was its plan to raise research and development spending to about four percent of revenues from three percent recently.
Mazda, the firth ranked Japanese car maker, posted a parent current profit of 2.08 billion yen in the six months ended September 30, 1996, after a string of losses.
Ford increased its stake in Mazda to one-third from 24.5 percent last April, giving it management control.
Later Wallace, a former Ford official seconded to Mazda, was appointed president, becoming the first foreigner to head a major Japenese firm.
